units: body px (parts/legacy/body.png px); dir/aim = screen deg, y down, 0 = right = FACING, -90 = up. All slots are canonical facing-right (side +1); `layer` front = near side (drawn over the body), back = far side (drawn behind it, dark arms + dark hands).
mirror: The figure faces its walking direction; when walking left OR when the target is behind (target x < anchor x in facing-right space), the WHOLE composed figure (body + every arm) is mirrored about the anchor x. Compose facing right with the target mirrored into facing-right space, then flip the result (compose_ref.MultiArm.frame(..., facing=-1)). Arms therefore only ever aim into the facing half-plane (aimClamp around the weapon rest aim).

raised.note: keys with raised:true on a FRONT-layer arm swap the arm for this painting (one piece, rotated by rrot about its shoulder) and draw the weapon at weaponZ (behind the body = behind the head); back-layer arms use the key's raise/elbow instead
raised.backNote: weapons_v2: back-layer slots on raised:true keys swap their arm for this dark painting (same rule as front: placed at the slot with shoulder on the slot, rotated by rrot; weapon through its grip at weaponZ). Before this, back slots dropped raised and used raise/elbow.

pass9: art pass 9 weapon spread (tools/pass9/spread_apply.py): sprouted slot pos/dir re-laid out, far native arm overridden for 2..6 weapons, per-slot rest wrist offsets baked into body_track (slots[*].pass9 lists them). Same schema; no code change needed for the spread.
